question: The Bhakra Nangal Dam is situated on which river?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sutlej**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on the **Sutlej River**, which is one of the five major rivers of the Punjab region.
 
• It is located in **Himachal Pradesh** and **Punjab**, India, and is one of the tallest gravity dams in the world, with a height of 226 meters.
 
• The dam was constructed in 1963 and is primarily used for **irrigation, power generation, and flood control**.
 
• The Bhakra Dam reservoir is known as the **"Gobind Sagar"**, named after Guru Gobind Singh, the 10th Sikh Guru.
 
• It contributes significantly to the hydroelectric power production in North India, providing electricity to states like Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Himachal Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yamuna**

 
 
• The Yamuna is the largest tributary of the Ganga River and originates from the **Yamunotri Glacier** in Uttarakhand.
 
• It flows through major cities such as Delhi, Agra, and Mathura.
 
• The river is considered sacred in Indian culture and is associated with various mythological and historical events.
 
• Despite its sacred status, the Yamuna is one of the most polluted rivers in India, particularly in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Ganga**
 
 
• The Ganga, also known as the Ganges, is India's most important and sacred river, originating from the **Gangotri Glacier** in Uttarakhand.
 
• It flows through the northern plains and empties into the Bay of Bengal, covering a length of over 2,500 km.
 
• The Ganga is a lifeline for millions, providing water for agriculture, industry, and domestic use.
 
• It is also central to Indian spirituality and culture, with numerous pilgrimage sites located along its banks.
 
 
 
• **Beas**
 
 
• The Beas River originates from the **Beas Kund** near Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• It flows for about 470 km before merging with the Sutlej River in Punjab.
 
• The river is historically significant as it marked the easternmost extent of Alexander the Great's conquest in India.
 
• The Beas is also used for irrigation and hydropower generation, with projects like the Pong Dam situated on it.
